related_synthesis_entries.claim: Rational kernels select boundary observables while generalized Littlewood residues express every zero to the right of b as a same-sign defect; the nominal equality holds exactly when that defect measure vanishes.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The kernel is a query posed to log zeta: its poles select explicit zeta data, its boundary trace supplies the desired weighted integral, and generalized Littlewood residues expose zeros to one side of the line. Designing the criterion is therefore largely designing a rational kernel whose remote contour edges vanish.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source integrates log zeta(z) against g(z)=1/(a^2-(z-b)^2) around a rectangle based on Re z=b. The left edge becomes a weighted log-zeta integral, the other three edges vanish as the rectangle expands, and residue/generalized Littlewood arguments express the result through kernel poles, zeta's pole, and zeros inside the contour. The note adapts this construction from log modulus to weighted arg zeta integrals.
directed.conceptual_reading: A single contour identity is a generator of criteria: kernel choice determines what boundary observable is measured and how zeros are weighted. It compresses a global zero-free statement into equality of an explicit baseline with a boundary integral plus signed corrections.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The rational kernel bridges analytic boundary data and the divisor of zeta. It exposes poles and zeros through residues while the contour limit forgets the remote edges after their decay is proved.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The construction only becomes an RH or half-strip criterion when the zero contributions have controlled sign and all contour-limit and branch-of-log conditions are justified. This introductory span states the mechanism, not each later criterion's full hypotheses.
directed.uncertainty: The method is prose-stable, but OCR degrades the exact kernel typography and contour orientation; exact formulas should be checked before transcription.

supported: The introduction explicitly defines the rational kernel, rectangular contour, left-edge weighted log-zeta integral, decay of the three remote edges, and evaluation by residues and generalized Littlewood theory.
It also states that the note adapts the method from log-modulus integrals to argument integrals.
inference: Describing kernel choice as selecting a boundary observable is a reasonable interpretation of the construction.
Branch and contour-limit obligations are reasonable analytic cautions even though the introduction does not spell them out.
